newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbian students protest in Belgrade for 24th day.
newsitem.headline: Serbian students protest in Belgrade for 24th day.

text.p: Thousands of students gathered in central Belgrade on Wednesday for street protests in what has become a daily routine of mass demonstrations against Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic.

Student leaders said 40,000 students were expected to join the protest march which would pass by the Yugoslav federal parliament. On Tuesday the assembly held its first session since disputed municipal elections in Belgrade on November 17 which the opposition says it won.
The Zajedno (Together) coalition of opposition parties accused parliament of rubber-stamping socialist vote fraud and boycotted the session.

The opposition's legal and administrative options against the reversal of their initially-reported election victory were exhausted on Tuesday when the Yugoslav supreme court refused to hear their appeal.

Zajedno, whose own daily protest march was due to start later on Wednesday, has asked for Western support in its bid to force Milosevic into accepting defeat and said it was counting on crucial trade union support for its campaign.

Leaders of the association of independent trade unions said at least 10,000 of their members were taking part in the daily student marches, but added their members were afraid to reveal their identities for fear of reprisals by management.
"They are afraid to march because they say their bosses will recognise them and they will be kicked out of the factory," a union official said.
The United States and other Western governments have backed the opposition, cautioning against the use of force and supporting their calls for the socialists to recognise Zajedno's win.
